The section covers the effect of electing an ineligible person and the offence for sitting or voting while disqualified.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address consequences where a disqualified or incapable person is elected or participates on council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that election of a disqualified or incapable person is void and that sitting or voting while disqualified is an offence.

reason: Section 74 separates officer appointment powers from tenure and dismissal protection.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify required and optional municipal offices and allow multiple offices in one person.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which municipal officers council must or may appoint and that one person may hold more than one office.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state tenure and dismissal-for-cause protection and one exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the tenure protection for full-time municipal officers and the section 19 resolution exception.

reason: The section gives one rule for chief administrative officer duties and powers as set by council.

evidenceText: has such duties and powers as the council prescribes by by-law or resolution

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single duties-and-powers statement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a city or town chief administrative officer has the duties and powers council prescribes by by-law or resolution.

reason: Section 76 separates clerk duties from the assistant clerk substitute role.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(1) lists the clerk’s meeting, record, seal, notice, signing, and assigned duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the clerk duties for council meetings, municipal records, by-laws, the seal, notices, documents, and assigned tasks.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(2) focuses on the assistant clerk’s direction and substitute powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an assistant clerk has the clerk’s powers and duties.

reason: Section 77 separates treasurer duties from the assistant treasurer substitute role.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(1) lists the treasurer’s chief financial and accounting duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the treasurer’s duties for municipal money, accounts, records, statements, insurance, advice, and assigned tasks.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(2) focuses on the assistant treasurer’s direction and substitute powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an assistant treasurer has the treasurer’s powers and duties.

reason: The section is a focused municipal cheque signing rule.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address cheque signatures and reproduced signatures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who signs municipal cheques with the treasurer and when required signatures may be reproduced.

reason: The section gives a single liability protection for treasurer payments made under council authority.

evidenceText: The treasurer is not liable for any money paid by him in accordance with a by-law or resolution of the council

proposedGroups.reason: The target is one liability rule for payments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the treasurer is not liable for money paid under a council by-law or resolution.

reason: Section 80 contains a solicitor qualification rule and a separate costs-recovery entitlement.

proposedGroups.reason: This subsection states who may be appointed or hold office as municipal solicitor.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipal solicitor must be a member of the Law Society of New Brunswick.

proposedGroups.reason: This subsection addresses the municipality’s entitlement to costs in actions and proceedings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipality may tax and collect lawful costs even where solicitor or counsel remuneration is paid by salary.

reason: The section states a single qualification rule for municipal engineers.

evidenceText: unless he is a registered professional engineer

proposedGroups.reason: The target is one qualification requirement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipal engineer must be a registered professional engineer.

reason: Section 82 separates auditor qualification and audit duties from Minister cancellation and appointment powers.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover qualification, duties, the March 1 deadline, and transmitting statements and report.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall auditor qualification, annual audit timing, and the duty to transmit certified financial statements and report to the Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister cancellation and appointment of auditor
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address cancelling unqualified or incapable auditors and appointing an auditor when needed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister cancels or appoints a municipal auditor and who pays the appointed auditor’s fees and expenses.

reason: The section is a focused acting-officer appointment rule.

evidenceText: it may appoint an acting officer if the officer is absent due to illness or any other reason or the office is vacant

proposedGroups.reason: The target states when council may appoint an acting officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council may appoint an acting officer for an absent officer or vacant office.

reason: Section 84 separates the bonding requirement and premiums from production, safekeeping, and reporting duties.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require annual bonding and municipal payment of premiums.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that each municipality must provide annual bonding by by-law and pay the premiums for bonds.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover bond production, safekeeping, and auditor reporting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when bonds must be produced to council, how they are kept for auditor inspection, and what the auditor reports.

reason: The section addresses councillor eligibility for municipal appointment or employment and the volunteer exception.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections cover resignation, non-involvement, and voluntary employment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an elected councillor is eligible for municipal appointment or employment and when volunteer employment is excluded.

reason: Section 85.1 separates indemnity entitlement from insurance, court approval, notice, and volunteer coverage.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal indemnity for members officers and employees
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state discretionary and mandatory indemnity rules for listed municipal persons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may receive municipal indemnity, the honest-good-faith and lawful-conduct conditions, and when indemnity is an entitlement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Insurance and court approval for indemnity
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover insurance, court orders, notice to interested persons, and volunteer services.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the insurance power, court approval process, notice rights, and volunteer inclusion for indemnity.

Section 87 contains fiscal-year, estimate, tax-base, rate-approval, and area-rate topics.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the fiscal year and annual estimate submission contents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipal fiscal year and what annual estimate, tax base, rate, tax imposition, and source information must be submitted.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address assessed value of real property owned by Canada.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister determines assessed value of Canadian Crown real property when computing the municipal tax base.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern revised estimates, Minister approval, and failure to pass a resolution.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how estimates are revised after non-approval and how Minister approval fixes the rate for Real Property Tax Act purposes.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address service variation rates, annexed area rates, and adjustment to keep the estimate amount unchanged.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when different municipal rates may be fixed for different areas or annexed property and how the base rate is adjusted.
